Dear Underwriting Team,

This letter serves to provide a detailed overview of Mr. Jeffery Anderson's medical history and current health status as of his most recent visits. I hope this information is helpful in your evaluation.

Mr. Anderson, born on July 10, 1957, has been under my care since his early adulthood, and I have had the opportunity to follow his medical history closely. He presents with a variety of health conditions, which are detailed below.

On September 4, 2025, Mr. Anderson visited the clinic regarding his cataracts. His blood pressure at the time was 145/95, and he weighed 240 pounds. Mr. Anderson has a known history of prediabetes, specifically impaired fasting glucose, which is currently controlled with an A1c level of 5.2. He is taking metformin 500 mg as part of his treatment regimen. Additionally, he has non-obstructive coronary artery disease, characterized by a 74% stenosis and a CAC score of 95. His erectile dysfunction, which began in November 2019, is also managed with tadalafil 20 mg. His family history includes breast cancer in his mother, who was diagnosed at the age of 43 and away at 55, and a stroke in his father, who passed away at 53. Mr. Anderson is a former smoker who quit in May 2021, having smoked one pack per day since June 2016. He drinks approximately eight alcoholic beverages per week.

During his visit on December 25, 2024, for an annual physical, Mr. Anderson's blood pressure was 135/87, and he weighed 234 pounds. His prediabetes remains well controlled with an A1c of 5.2. His non-obstructive coronary artery disease and erectile dysfunction are stable and the same medications as before. His cataracts are also under control. Socially, his smoking history and alcohol consumption remain unchanged.

On April 15, 2024, Mr. Anderson returned follow-up regarding his cataracts. His blood pressure was 137/91, and he weighed 237 pounds. His A1c was and his non-obstructive coronary artery disease and erectile dysfunction remained stable. His medications and lifestyle factors were consistent with previous visits.

Mr. Anderson's initial presentation for his coronary artery disease was on August 5, 2023. At that time, his blood pressure was 136/95, and he weighed 230 pounds. His A1c was 5.3 at that visit, but it has since been brought down to an average of 5.2. His cataracts and erectile dysfunction were also noted at this visit. His family history, smoking history, and alcohol consumption were documented as above.
